title: Workdays Calculator – Count Working Days Between Two Dates (Free)
shortDescription: Count business days between two dates, excluding weekends and any holidays you list. Customizable: include Saturday or Sunday as workdays if needed.
description: Choose Date range to count working days between two dates, or 'N workdays from a date' to find a future or past workday. Customize weekends, 2026–2027 US/UK/Japan/Germany holiday presets and your own dates; the start day is excluded in the N-workdays mode.
metaDescription: Enter a start and end date to get the number of working days instantly. Skips weekends and US, UK, Japan or Germany holidays, or your own list. Free tool.

sections.heading: Why workday counting matters
paragraphs: Project deadlines, contract terms, payroll cycles, and leave planning all use 'business days' rather than calendar days. A delivery promise of 30 business days made on a Friday is actually 42 calendar days because weekends don't count. Mistaking the two leads to missed deadlines and contract disputes.

Workdays also matter for legal counting: in many jurisdictions, statutory time limits (e.g., '14 business days to respond') exclude weekends and public holidays. Always check whether 'days' means calendar or business in any agreement.

sections.heading: Why we let you customize weekends
paragraphs: Most countries use Saturday-Sunday as the weekend, but it varies. Most Middle Eastern and some North African countries observe Friday-Saturday as the weekend. Some industries (retail, hospitality) consider weekends as workdays.

You can include Saturday or Sunday as workdays with the toggles, or leave both as weekends (the default). These controls cannot make Friday a weekend, so a Friday–Saturday weekend is not modeled directly here. For legal or contractual deadlines, verify the applicable local calendar rather than relying on this toggle alone.

sections.heading: How to use the holidays input
paragraphs: Paste a list of dates in YYYY-MM-DD format (ISO 8601). Separators can be commas, spaces, or newlines. Each date you list will be excluded from the workday count if it falls on what would otherwise be a workday.

The holiday preset above covers the United States, Japan, the United Kingdom (England & Wales) and Germany for 2026–2027. For other countries, regional holidays or company closures, list the dates here — they are added on top of the preset.

faq.q: How many workdays are between two dates?
faq.a: Enter both dates: the calculator counts every Monday–Friday in the range (start and end included), then subtracts the public holidays from the preset you pick and any dates you list. Example: July 1–31, 2026 has 23 weekdays; with the US federal holiday preset (Independence Day observed on Friday, July 3) it is 22 workdays.

faq.q: How do I find the date that is N workdays after a start date?
faq.a: Use the 'N workdays from a date' mode on this calculator, enter a start date and signed number of workdays (negative for earlier dates), then choose the same weekend settings, holiday preset and any custom holiday dates. The start date itself is not counted. All listed custom holidays are applied here; you do not need to transfer them to another calculator. To double-check a positive N, switch to Date range and count from the day after your start date through the result (inclusive) with the same settings.

faq.q: Are start and end dates inclusive?
faq.a: Yes. A start or end date is counted only if it is a workday after applying your weekend and holiday settings. If you need only dates strictly between them, subtract each distinct endpoint that was actually counted (0, 1 or 2), not always 2. For the same start and end date, the exclusive result is 0. Or select 'Exclude start and end dates' in Date range to calculate this automatically.

Only if you pick a preset: built-in data covers public holidays in the United States, Japan, the United Kingdom (England & Wales) and Germany for 2026–2027. Holidays vary by country, region and year, so for anywhere else — or for company-specific days off — add the dates manually; they are combined with the preset.

faq.q: Can I use this for international contracts?
faq.a: Yes — but make sure both parties agree on which holidays to count. Multinational contracts often specify 'business days as observed in the [city] of [country]' to avoid ambiguity.

faq.q: What if a holiday falls on a weekend?
faq.a: It's not double-counted. If 2026-01-01 is a Thursday holiday, it's counted as a holiday. If 2027-12-25 falls on a Saturday, the algorithm correctly counts it as one day (weekend), not two.

faq.q: How does this work for a 6-day work week?
faq.a: Check 'Saturday is a workday'. The calculator will count Mon-Sat as workdays and only exclude Sundays and listed holidays.

faq.q: What's the maximum date range I can compute?
faq.a: Hundreds of years at minimum. The browser handles date arithmetic up to ±100 million days from 1970.

faq.q: Can I export the workday list?
faq.a: Not as a download, but you can copy the displayed numbers. For a per-day list, a spreadsheet is more flexible.

faq.q: Does the data leave my browser?
faq.a: No. Everything runs locally; nothing is sent to a server.
